Respect at King’s Academy College Park means valuing every individual, treating others with fairness and inclusivity, and maintaining high expectations while supporting growth.

Kid's Club - Wraparound Childcare
Kid's Club provides before and after school childcare for children attending King's Academy College Park.
The club operates term time only, from 7.30am to 5.30pm, and provides children with a safe, welcoming environment to play and relax before and after the school day.
Registration is required before your child can attend. Sessions are booked and paid for through Scopay.
For full information about Kid's Club, please read our information booklet.

If you have any questions, please contact the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - King's Academy College Park
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
A very warm welcome to King’s Academy College Park.
As the Headteacher, I am immensely proud to lead a school where we value each individual and seek to encourage everyone to reach their full potential. Built on a strong foundation of respect, fairness, and inclusivity, our academy maintains the highest expectations and aspirations for both our pupils and staff. We celebrate every success while cultivating the resilience our children need to reflect on mistakes as vital opportunities to learn and grow.
We are incredibly proud of our vibrant community here on Portsea Island. As a school deeply rooted in Portsmouth’s unique maritime heritage and close-knit island identity, we are dedicated to broadening horizons. Our mission is to equip all our pupils with the confidence, knowledge, and values they need to thrive - not just here at home, but on a global stage.
Our Promise to Every Child
Through our unified approach across the Early Years, Key Stage 1, and Key Stage 2, we ensure that every King’s Academy College Park pupil benefits from:
Working in Partnership
We firmly believe that education is a shared journey. We are deeply appreciative of our relationships with our parents, carers, and the local Portsmouth community. By building a positive, supportive partnership with you, we can ensure our school continuously improves and paves the way for our pupils' bright futures.
Whether you are an existing family or looking to join our community, we look forward to working hand-in-hand with you to support your child's growth, character, and success.

Attendance
Our parents are an important part of our School community, working together with the staff and children to make King's Academy College Park a safe and happy place to learn.
Regular school attendance is important for your child's learning, wellbeing and friendships. Every school day matters – moments matter, attendance counts.
We want all children at King's Academy College Park to feel safe, happy and supported to attend school every day. We understand that sometimes children may find coming to school difficult. If you have concerns about your child's attendance, please talk to us so that we can work together to understand any barriers and identify the right support.
How can I support my child's attendance?
Establish regular morning and bedtime routines.
If your child is struggling to come to school
Sometimes children can become worried or anxious about attending school. Please speak to us as soon as possible if this is happening. Working together with families, we can help identify what is making attendance difficult and put appropriate support in place.
Please don't wait until attendance becomes a concern – talk to us early.
When should my child stay at home?
If your child is unwell, please follow the NHS and public health guidance on when they should stay at home.
Vomiting or diarrhoea: Your child must stay at home until 48 hours after the last episode to help prevent illness spreading to others.
For further information, please see the NHS Guidance 'Is my child too ill for school?'
Reporting an absence
If your child is unable to attend school, please let us know by 9:00am on the morning of their absence. You can report absence via Studybugs.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Meals - King's Academy College Park
pageCache.text:
School Meals
Our school meals
Our school meals are freshly prepared on site and offer a choice of nutritious and balanced meals each day. Our menu operates on a three-week rota and includes three hot meal choices, as well as a sandwich option. You can view our current menus below.
How much do school meals cost?
Reception, Year 1 & Year 2: School meals are free for all children
Years 3 - 6: School meals cost £2.96 per meal, payable via Scopay
Free School Meals: Your child may be eligible for benefits-related Free School Meals.
Check your eligibility and apply through Portsmouth City Council, even if your child is already receiving universal free school meals.
Allergies and dietary requirements
Please inform the school if your child had a food allergy, food intolerance or other dietary requirement. It is important that we are made aware of any dietary requirements before your child has a school meal so that appropriate arrangements can be put in place with our catering team.

Uniform
We have 2 uniform suppliers, Price & Buckland and Hargreaves Promotions, please click on either logo to visit their website.
Second-hand uniform
We always appreciate the generosity of our community in donating second-hand school uniform to us. These donations not only support many of our families but also promote sustainability within our school community.
From time to time, we hold second-hand uniform sales, offering an affordable option for families to purchase uniforms while giving pre-loved items a new lease of life.
If you have any used uniform to donate or would like to learn more about our upcoming sales, please contact the school office.
HIVE Portsmouth
HIVE Portsmouth’s Uniform Share Store helps families across the city by getting children and young people kitted out in their school uniform. Constantly having to buy new uniform including school shoes, PE kit, items with logos and other essentials means that costs can soon mount up. This can add to the financial pressure on parents, especially in these challenging times.
Their Uniform Share Store can help. It boasts hundreds of good quality uniform items, both second-hand and new. They have all been sorted and stored, ready to be worn. Not only does the scheme save families money, it’s also great for the environment – particularly given the rate at which children grow!
Simply email uniform@hiveportsmouth.org.uk or fill in the form on their website and their team will put together your order and arrange a convenient day and time for collection from Central Library, Guildhall Square.
They are always very grateful for donations of good quality pre-loved school uniform. Items can be dropped off at any Portsmouth library during opening hours. Simply pop the clothes in a bag marked 'for HIVE Portsmouth' and your items will make their way to us.
Why do we have a uniform?
We believe that having a school uniform can play a key role in:
Promoting the ethos of a school Providing a sense of belonging and identity Setting an appropriate tone for education
Our uniform also promotes our identity as a part of King's Group Academies.
It is incredibly important to us for the uniform to act as a social leveller, which is why we are asking for no branding/logos (e.g. Nike, Adidas etc) on items of clothing worn into school. These items should be reserved for wearing outside the school.
As you can imagine, for a school of our size, labelling of all clothing is vital.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum Overview - King's Academy College Park
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Overview
At King's Academy College Park, our curriculum is thoroughly planned to provide a broad and balanced education that meets the needs of all pupils. This gives them the skills, knowledge and understanding along with essential attributes to take part positively and actively in society and to prepare them for a successful future.
We want to ensure that our pupils receive an enriched and progressive curriculum and that learning is challenging, aspirational, relevant and exciting. For our pupils, most of whom have been born and brought up in and around the populated area of the city of Portsmouth, we believe that it is a priority that they develop skills and knowledge in core curriculum subjects. This is to ensure that our pupils leave us with high levels of literacy and numeracy to enable social mobility, greater potential to attend further and higher education and be more successful in life.
When planning the curriculum, teachers always take into consideration the children’s starting point to understand what prior learning may have already been undertaken. We understand that a child’s ability to learn is based on gaining knowledge and building on learnt knowledge; as well as the ability to use and apply associated skills adeptly and competently. They can then build on what they know already to provide first-hand experiences, allowing the children to develop interpersonal skills, build resilience and become creative, critical thinkers.
